clue.text: Comic character finally meets hero, breaking arm

indicators.note: breaking up a set of letters smashes their order, so the pooled pieces are rearranged

parts.note: a wit is a comic, someone who makes jokes
Z is the final character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: In a comic strip, the last character to appear meets the hero and breaks his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges WIT, Z and HERO together. 'arm' looks like a body part but means a weapon, as in firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a big field gun firing shells at a high angle is one such weapon.

clue.text: Poor main road by university overwhelmed by horsepower

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, so the outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: HP is the abbreviation for horsepower
A is a main road in Britain and RD the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A main road near a university is swamped by powerful cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' puts A, RD and U inside HP. British main roads are numbered A-roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money is being poor.

clue.text: Caribbean criminals inside offend somewhere in US

parts.note: WI stands for West Indies, the Caribbean islands

indicators.note: inside means the criminals are placed within the word for offend

parts.note: to sin is to offend against a moral law
cons are convicts, criminals

explanation.surface: Caribbean criminals cause offence somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' doubles as slang for being in prison, which suits the criminals in the surface. WI, for West Indies, is the usual crossword shorthand for the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern state is one place within the country.

clue.text: Invite politician to join treaty, periodically

indicators.note: to join means the politician enters the middle of the other letters
periodically means at regular intervals, so alternate letters of treaty are taken

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone invites a politician to sign up to a treaty from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' picks every other letter starting from the first; 'to join' is a loose way of saying the politician goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone is to invite them to do something.

clue.text: Following outbreak of fear, friend raises protective headgear

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of fear are rearranged
raises means lifts up, and in a down clue that turns the word round

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: After a scare, a friend puts on protective headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak of' rearranges fear and 'raises' lifts pal upward, as a down entry reads top to bottom. 'Following' only tells you the friend comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap on a cap that folds down over the ears protects them from cold.

clue.text: Old boy's retiring cricket team no good — game full of sloggers

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters for old boy are read backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a cricket side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A former pupil leaves a poor cricket side whose matches are full of big hitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the old boy round. 'sloggers' suggests cricket batsmen in this cricket surface, but here it means boxers who slug away.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers trade heavy punches, so the sport is fairly described as one full of people who slog at each other.

clue.text: Jack-of-all-trades lifted party, playing banjo with MD

indicators.note: lifted means raised, and in a down clue that reverses the word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handyman lifts the party mood by playing the banjo with a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns DO to OD and 'playing' mixes BANJO and MD into DJOBMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman who does all sorts of small tasks is a jack-of-all-trades.

clue.text: Ancient tribe freeze in retreats

parts.note: ice is frozen water, to freeze is to ice

indicators.note: retreats means goes back, so the word in is reversed

explanation.surface: An ancient tribe freezes in its retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns IN to NI. Boudicca led this tribe against Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: This people of eastern England rebelled against Roman rule.

clue.text: Soldier, bloody after fall northwards, became inarticulate

indicators.note: after means the colour comes behind the reversed piece

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: northwards means going up, which in a down clue reverses the word

parts.note: to ebb is to fall away, as a tide does
blood is red

explanation.surface: A soldier, bloodied after a fall, can only babble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses fall because this is a down entry, read upward; 'after' sets the bloody colour behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk fast and without sense is to fail to speak clearly.

clue.text: Cooked oyster has no time to take back butter flavouring

indicators.note: to take means the shuffled letters hold another piece inside them
cooked means prepared or altered, so the letters are rearranged
has no means a letter is removed from the word oyster
back means the word for butter is read in reverse

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A recipe: a cooked oyster with no time to spare, finished with butter for flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' drops the time, 'Cooked' shuffles what is left, 'back' turns the butter round and 'to take' sets it inside. 'butter' is the animal that butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is used to flavour roast meats and stews.

clue.text: Braved storms, foolishly maybe

indicators.note: storms suggests violent upheaval, so the letters of braved are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone braved the storms, perhaps unwisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' rearranges BRAVED. The definition is by example: foolishly is a word of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolishly is a word that modifies a verb, an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: Having two pints, Roger, with temperature, off colour

indicators.note: off means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: a quart is two pints
R is radio code for roger, message received

explanation.surface: After two pints someone is feeling a bit off colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes R and T from A QUART. 'off colour' reads as unwell but splits into the signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This light blue-green is a shade, from the Latin for water.

clue.text: In empty Utrecht stole foreign vessel

indicators.note: In means one piece is placed inside the other
empty means the word Utrecht loses all but its first and last letters

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf or stole

explanation.surface: Someone in Utrecht steals a foreign ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the first and last letters of Utrecht; 'In' sets the scarf between them. 'stole' looks like a verb but is the scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine was a vessel from a foreign navy.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink on the rocks? It has medicinal properties

parts.note: liquor is any alcoholic drink
a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: Is a strong drink served with ice good for your health?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' is the barman's phrase for a drink poured over ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of this plant has long been used as a remedy for coughs and digestion.

clue.text: Cowboy outside heads for site, constructing steep slope

indicators.note: outside means the name of the cowboy wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the American Wild West

indicators.note: heads for means the first letters of site and constructing are taken

explanation.surface: A cowboy works outside on a building site, putting up a steep bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' gives S and C, and 'outside' puts EARP round them.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification this is the inner wall of a ditch, and more generally a sheer bank or cliff.

clue.text: Old rocker, top model, made in France, had a flawed exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the rearranged letters form an outer shell round the French word
flawed means imperfect, so the letters are rearranged
top means the first letter of model

parts.note: fait is French for made

explanation.surface: An old rock star with a top model made in France had a flawed outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' gives the first letter of model, 'flawed' mixes it with the letters of 'had a', and 'exterior' wraps the result round the French word. 'top model' tempts as a supermodel's name.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a British pop singer of the late 1950s and 60s, so a veteran of rock and roll.

clue.text: Author reviewed animal experiment's source

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again in a new way, so the letters of animal are rearranged
source means the beginning, so the first letter of experiment is taken

explanation.surface: A writer reviews where an animal experiment came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' shuffles ANIMAL, and 'source' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the stories of a bear called Pooh, so he is a famous writer.

clue.text: Can boxer, with extraneous kilos start to enhance image?

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: extraneous means lying outside, so the kilos stand on either side of the boxer

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for a kilo, so two kilos give two
Muhammad Ali was a world heavyweight boxing champion

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of enhance

explanation.surface: Can a boxer carrying extra weight improve his image?
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraneous' puts the two Ks outside ALI and 'start to' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: A double, someone who closely resembles another, is that person's image.

clue.text: Massive house, with parking for two, flanked by annexe

indicators.note: flanked by means the outer word sits on both sides of the rest

parts.note: a wing is an extension or annexe of a building
P is the symbol for parking, given twice

explanation.surface: A huge house with a double parking space and an annexe on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanked by' means the annexe sits on both sides; 'for two' doubles the parking sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whopping is enormous, huge in size.

clue.text: Russian leader, scratching head in writing government reports

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: one's hand is one's handwriting

indicators.note: scratching head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the tsar was the ruler of imperial Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian leader scratches his head while writing reports for the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' removes the ruler's first letter and 'in' puts what is left inside the handwriting. The surface suggests a puzzled tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official printed record of debates in the UK Parliament.

clue.text: Determined to make diversion, avoiding centre of Exeter

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so letters are removed from the diversion

parts.note: a detour is a diversion off the usual route

indicators.note: centre of means the two middle letters of Exeter

explanation.surface: Determined to take a diversion round the middle of Exeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives ET, the middle of six-letter Exeter, and 'avoiding' takes it out of DETOUR. Exeter is a city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A dour person is stern and stubborn, hence determined.

clue.text: Messenger initially overrun by company vehicles

indicators.note: initially overrun means the first letter of the word is run over and lost

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger sent on a mission

explanation.surface: A messenger is overrun at first by a firm's vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially overrun' removes the first letter of the messenger; 'by' simply places it next to the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of vehicles travelling together is called this.

clue.text: Tropical plant idiot coated with sparkling wine

indicators.note: coated with means covered, so the wine wraps round the idiot

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A tropical plant: an idiot drenched in fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coated with' puts the idiot inside the wine. Cava is Spain's sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy root crop, also called manioc, grows in the tropics.

clue.text: Military officer called for nuts and bolts

indicators.note: called means spoken aloud, so the officer's title is heard

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A colonel is summoned for the essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' tells you the officer's title is spoken; colonel is pronounced like this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or essence of something, its basic workings, is its nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Outdated tackle causes foul- Spurs get rattled

indicators.note: get rattled means shaken up, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A football match: a foul, and the Spurs players get rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get rattled' shuffles FOUL and SPURS. 'tackle' means gear, not a football challenge; Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggy golfing knickerbockers are old-fashioned clothing, and tackle can mean outfit or equipment.

clue.text: Dreadful ceremony banishing some source of evil

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Dreadful ceremony banishing some source of evil', gives no parse for ULCER: the likely wordplay is an anagram of LUCRE, money as source of evil, but the clue appears garbled and no scan or blog confirms it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dreadful ceremony banishing some source of evil

clue.text: Charming, except when catching tube

indicators.note: catching means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: save can mean except, as in all save one
U stands for the Underground, London's tube railway

explanation.surface: Being charming except when you are stuck on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts U inside SAVE. London's tube is the Underground, often abbreviated to U on signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smooth and polished in manner is charming.

clue.text: Army book about weapon

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An army book about weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is the usual abbreviation for the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved cavalry sword is a weapon.

clue.text: Italian island saving imprisoned character from Greece

indicators.note: imprisoned means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: an ISA is a UK Individual Savings Account
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: On an Italian island, a Greek is rescued from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' puts the Greek letter inside the savings account. An ISA is a tax-free UK savings account, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: This volcanic island lies in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: College barman organised drinks first in induction period

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so one piece swallows the other
organised means put into order, so the letters of barman are rearranged
first in means the opening letter of induction is used

explanation.surface: At a college, the barman organises drinks for the first night of induction week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns BARMAN into AMBRAN, 'first in' gives I, and 'drinks' puts I inside after C. 'period' means a span of geological time.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the earliest geological span of the Palaeozoic era, so it is a period in that sense.

clue.text: Serviceman perhaps felt restored by constant laughing

indicators.note: restored, read as stored back, tells you to turn the word round

parts.note: felt is a matted cloth, used here for a rug made of it
K is the symbol for a constant in science
ha is the sound of laughing

explanation.surface: A soldier feels better after a long laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' is read as stored back, a reversal. Both that signal and felt for a rug are loose, which makes this the hardest clue here.
explanation.definitionFit: These Nepalese soldiers serve in the British Army, so one is an example of a serviceman.

clue.text: Tart from London area showing rear to everyone during dance

indicators.note: during means within, so the other pieces go inside the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
Kew is a district of south-west London, home to famous gardens

indicators.note: rear to means the last letter of everyone

explanation.surface: A tart from London shows her bottom to everyone at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear to' takes the last letter of everyone and 'during' sets it, after the London district, inside the dance. 'Tart' tempts a rude reading; it is the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond and jam pastry, named after a Derbyshire town, is a well-known British tart.
